text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm planning a benchmark pass focused on long-context and mixed-context workloads. Need to lock down methodology before we run large Dedicated pools. Thoughts?

dan: +1. Are we talking synthetic load or replayed user traffic?

maria: Both. We need apples-to-apples comparisons between kernels/batching configs. Also want to measure prefill-dominant vs decode-dominant workloads separately.

ryan: For apples-to-apples: same model binary, same tokenizer, same seed, same input distribution. Only change runtime knobs. Otherwise results are noisy.

tess: Agree. Also document the KV cache state: cold vs warm. Long-context perf is very sensitive to whether KV is populated from prefill.

maria: Proposed test matrix:
- Replay harness (session-level) for realistic mixes
- Synthetic client with controlled seq-length distribution for edge cases
- Two workload classes: prefill-heavy (e.g., single 8k prefill + 256 decode) and streaming-heavy (many short prefill+decode pairs)
- Kernel variants: default fused attention, cuBLAS fallback, int8/quantized path
- Batching heuristics: static batch sizes vs adaptive continuous batching

dan: Add percentiles (p50/p95/p99 tail) and breakdowns by prefill vs decode time. We should also report tokens/sec and GPU utl.

oliver: I'm going to add system-level profiling: nvprof/NSYS traces for representative runs, plus host-side CPU timelines. That will help explain kernel selection differences.

maria: For replay harness — aim to capture per-request: session id, user timestamp, token counts (prefill/decode), random seed, and exact prompt bytes. We'll replay in-order to preserve KV reuse.

dan: Important: when replaying, we must not accidentally reroute to model variants. Pin model version and force single-device placement.

perf-bot: Reminder: benchmarks must be reproducible. Upload config JSON and seed to /perf/bench-configs and tag PR.

tess: About batching heuristics — we should run with two modes:
1) Continuous batching tuned for latency SLO (autobatch window small)
2) Throughput mode (larger window, higher token throughput) 
Compare both across long-context.

maria: Also want to isolate kernel selection policy impact. Proposal:
- Run with kernel selector enabled (runtime picks kernels)
- Run with selector pinned to each kernel variant
Record selected kernel per layer / seq-length.

dan: We need to capture per-layer timings and KV memory traffic. KV behavior: measure per-step memcpy/PCIe moves vs GPU local access. For private deployments, include HBM pressure metrics.

oliver: I'll add a light-weight metric exporter that emits per-step: layer, kernel name, time_us, kv_hits, kv_bytes. We can scrape that into the perf dashboard.

maria: For apples-to-apples fairness, ensure tokenizer outputs same length: include a step to validate tokenization parity with a checksum per prompt.

tess: Good call. Also add a prefill-only baseline: run only prefill with no decode to measure worst-case prefill time and kernel scaling across seq_len.

dan: Let's define synthetic distributions:
- Uniform-Short: 64 +/- 16 tokens
- Long-Tail: 128/512/2048/8192 with probs [0.6,0.2,0.15,0.05]
- Prefill-Dominant: single prefill 8192 then N=32 decodes of 8 tokens

maria: Nice. We'll run each distribution at multiple QPS points to map latency curves and identify knee points where batching starts hurting tails.

perf-bot: Suggested nomenclature for artifacts: <date>-<dist>-<kernel>-<batchmode>-<seed>.trace.json

ryan: Action items:
- oliver: implement exporter + NSYS config (eta 2d)
- dan: expand replay harness to include prefill-dominant sessions and token checksums (eta 3d)
- tess: run initial small-scale runs on dev cluster and post results (eta EOD)
- maria: write benchmark runbook and perf dashboard queries (eta 2d)

maria: One more point — regression detection: after baseline, run new changes and require no >10% increase in prefill p95 and no regression in tokens/sec for throughput targets. Flagged runs create alert in #eng-runtime.

dan: For analysis, correlate kernel choice with regression windows. Often regressions show up when selector switches to fallback kernel at specific seq lengths.

tess: I'll start an initial thread with EOD pilot results. Keep notes brief so we have an audit trail.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone finds a corner-case workload we missed (e.g., many short prefill bursts in parallel), add it to the matrix. :eyes: 

ryan: FYI I'll reserve a small Dedicated pool for a repeatable run once we have the runbook.

perf-bot: Run scheduled: 1724509950 by @tess on dev cluster (auto-notify on completion).
